Acme Integrations: hey team — after we switched our embedding pipeline to `embed-lite-v2` the rerank results look totally off. No 400 or schema error, just weird scores (near-zero and some negatives). We send embeddings produced by our batch job straight to /v1/rerank. example payload attached below (trimmed):

```json
{
  "query_embedding": [0.012, -0.03, 0.45, 0.001, ...],
  "candidate_embeddings": [
    [0.002, 0.11, 0.4, -0.02, ...],
    [0.9, -0.4, 0.01, 0.3, ...]
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "embedding_model": "embed-lite-v2",
    "rerank_model": "rerank-alpha-1"
  }
}
```

We looked at dims locally: query length = 1024, candidate length = 1024, but we believe `rerank-alpha-1` historically used 1536. Not sure how to debug further. Any quick checks?

Maya (Support): thanks — can you paste the exact first 8 numbers for both the query and one candidate (no PII) and the request_id if possible? Also which endpoint URL/version are you hitting (hosted vs dedicated)?

Acme Integrations: pasted below. We're hitting the hosted API at `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank` with our org key. Request id in response header `x-request-id: rq_abc123`. Example first 8 dims: query `[0.012,-0.031,0.451,0.001,-0.0004,0.21,0.004, -0.12]`, candidate 1 `[0.002,0.110,0.401,-0.019,0.0003,0.205,-0.002,-0.118]`. We run everything as floats (not strings).

Alex (Eng): quick notes — reranker backend historically expects vectors from the same model family. If dims differ we used to return 400, but a change in 2025 allowed lenient handling (zero-pad/truncate) for mixed inputs for some routes to be tolerant. That can make dot-product scores meaningless if models aren't aligned. Can you run a single-call repro? e.g.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v2","input":"test"}' | jq
```

and then call rerank with that exact vector as query and one candidate produced by `rerank-alpha-1` to see the score. If you can share the two raw vectors and `x-request-id` I can look up the internal trace.

Priya (ML): additional heads-up — two separate failure modes here: 1) if embeddings are from different model spaces (different dimensionality or different training objectives) dot-product/cosine is not a valid comparison. 2) if one model returns L2-normalized embeddings and the other doesn’t, cosine vs dot will flip ordering. Our rerank endpoint defaults to `score_method: dot` unless `score_method: cosine` is specified. If your embed-lite-v2 changed normalization, that explains the jump. Workarounds: either produce embeddings with the same model as the reranker, or explicitly normalize before sending and use `score_method: cosine`.

Jordan (SRE): I pulled the logs for `rq_abc123` — server saw payload and executed rerank handler. No internal exception. The handler currently does a dimension check but if metadata `embedding_model` is present we skip strict validation (legacy compatibility). That's why there's no 4xx. I can see the vectors were length 1024 and the reranker weights expect 1536. The code path zero-pads the shorter vector to 1536 which leads to unpredictable dot products.

Maya (Support): action items: 1) Acme, please run Alex's single-call repro and paste both raw vectors + `rq_abc123`. 2) We'll open an internal bug to add stricter validation and a clear 400 when mixing incompatible dims without explicit opt-in. 3) temporary workaround: use the same embedding model as the reranker or run client-side conversion to the reranker model (not ideal).

Acme Integrations: repro done, dropped vectors and `rq_abc123` in the secure link (private). Score dropped from 0.87 to 0.00012 after the switch. We didn't realize the change in embed model would break things — our pipeline assumed embeddings were interchangeable.

Priya (ML): thanks — that delta is exactly what you'd expect if one vector space is 1024-d and another 1536-d and you're using raw dot product. If you want immediate parity, either: 1) regenerate candidates with `embed-lite-v2`, 2) call our hosted embeddings with `embed-pro-1` to match `rerank-alpha-1`, or 3) normalize vectors client-side and use `score_method: cosine` (only valid if both models are same or roughly compatible). We'll add docs clarifying this.

ticket-bot: created internal ticket `INTERNAL-1842` (label: rerank-dim-validation) assigned to eng/runtime.

Alex (Eng): I opened a small PR to opt-in to strict validation by default for hosted customers; we'll add a warning header `x-rerank-dim-warning` when automatic padding/truncation occurs and return 400 when `strict=true`. ETA for canary: 2 business days.

Maya (Support): follow-up for Acme — I added a support note with suggested immediate mitigation. Also sending a one-off support credit for the hours lost. Sorry for the surprise. :

Acme Integrations: thanks everyone, the workaround of using the same embed model fixed top-K ordering. Appreciate the quick investigation. :+1:

Jordan (SRE): we'll also add better traceability in logs (include embedding_model in traces) so these things are faster to triage.

Maya (Support): closing loop here — if you see anything else ping this thread or reopen `INTERNAL-1842`. Marking as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
